```{r pressure, include=FALSE}
# exploring the data
raw_2018 <- read.csv("data/AQ_2018.csv", check.names = FALSE)
names(raw_2018)
head(raw_2018)
head(raw_2018, 6)

# Function: clean_air_quality
# Purpose: Reads and cleans one year's air quality data.
# Arguments: 
## file: Path to the CSV file containing raw air quality measurements.
## ozone_units: Desired units for ozone concentration. Original ozone measurements are in ppm. Options are "ppm" or "ppb".
# Returns: A cleaned data frame containing one row per day with average daily concentrations of CO, PM2.5, and ozone.

clean_air_quality <- function(file, ozone_units = "ppm") {

  # Read the CSV file
  data <- read.csv(file, check.names = FALSE)

  # Convert the date column to correct date format
  data$Date <- as.Date(data$Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")

  # Select and rename the date and pollutant columns
  data <- data.frame(
    Date = data$Date,
    CO = data[["Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration"]],
    PM2.5 = data[["Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration"]],
    O3 = data[["Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration"]]
  )

  # Replace negative pollutant measurements with zero
  pollutant_columns <- c("CO", "PM2.5", "O3")

  for (i in pollutant_columns) {
    data[[i]][data[[i]] < 0] <- 0
  }

  # Calculate average pollutant concentrations for each day
  daily_data <- aggregate(
    . ~ Date,
    data = data,
    FUN = mean,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  # Convert ozone from ppm to ppb if requested
  if (ozone_units == "ppb") {
    daily_data$O3 <- daily_data$O3 * 1000
  }

  # Rename columns to make units clear
  names(daily_data) <- c(
    "Date", "CO", "PM2.5",
    paste0("O3_", ozone_units)
  )

  # Return the cleaned daily dataset
  return(daily_data)
}


# testing the function for 2018 dataset
aq_2018 <- clean_air_quality(
  file = "data/AQ_2018.csv",
  ozone_units = "ppm"
)

head(aq_2018)
str(aq_2018)
print(head(aq_2018, 6))

# Check total number of observations
nrow(air_quality_all)
```

```{r include=FALSE}
# Calculate yearly minimum and maximum concentrations
yearly_summary <- aggregate(
  cbind(CO, PM2.5, O3_ppm) ~ format(Date, "%Y"),
  data = air_quality_all,
  FUN = function(x) c(
    Min = min(x),
    Max = max(x)
  )
)

# Convert summary results into separate columns
yearly_summary_df <- data.frame(
  Year = yearly_summary[, 1],
  CO_Min = yearly_summary$CO[, "Min"],
  CO_Max = yearly_summary$CO[, "Max"],
  PM25_Min = yearly_summary$PM2.5[, "Min"],
  PM25_Max = yearly_summary$PM2.5[, "Max"],
  O3_Min = yearly_summary$O3_ppm[, "Min"],
  O3_Max = yearly_summary$O3_ppm[, "Max"]
)

# Create a separate formatted table for each year
yearly_tables <- lapply(unique(yearly_summary_df$Year), function(year) {

  yearly_summary_df %>%
    filter(Year == year) %>%
    select(-Year) %>%
    tbl_summary(
      type = everything() ~ "continuous",
      statistic = everything() ~ "{mean}",
      digits = everything() ~ 3,
      label = list(
        CO_Min ~ "CO Minimum (ppm)",
        CO_Max ~ "CO Maximum (ppm)",
        PM25_Min ~ "PM2.5 Minimum (µg/m³)",
        PM25_Max ~ "PM2.5 Maximum (µg/m³)",
        O3_Min ~ "O3 Minimum (ppm)",
        O3_Max ~ "O3 Maximum (ppm)"
      ),
      missing = "no"
    ) %>%
    modify_header(
      label = "**Pollutant measurement**"
    ) %>%
    modify_caption(
      paste0("**Yearly Minimum and Maximum Daily Pollutant Concentrations: ", year, "**")
    )
})
```

```{r include=FALSE}
# Calculate monthly mean concentrations and sample sizes
monthly_data <- air_quality_all %>%
  mutate(Month = lubridate::month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE)) %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(
    CO_mean = mean(CO),
    CO_sd = sd(CO),
    CO_n = n(),
    O3_mean = mean(O3_ppm),
    O3_sd = sd(O3_ppm),
    O3_n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate 95% confidence intervals
monthly_data <- monthly_data %>%
  mutate(
    CO_lower = CO_mean - 1.96 * CO_sd / sqrt(CO_n),
    CO_upper = CO_mean + 1.96 * CO_sd / sqrt(CO_n),
    O3_lower = O3_mean - 1.96 * O3_sd / sqrt(O3_n),
    O3_upper = O3_mean + 1.96 * O3_sd / sqrt(O3_n)
  )

# View monthly summary
monthly_data

# Combine CO and ozone summaries for plotting
monthly_plot_data <- bind_rows(
  monthly_data %>%
    transmute(
      Month,
      Pollutant = "Carbon Monoxide (CO)",
      Mean = CO_mean,
      Lower = CO_lower,
      Upper = CO_upper
    ),
  monthly_data %>%
    transmute(
      Month,
      Pollutant = "Ozone (O3)",
      Mean = O3_mean,
      Lower = O3_lower,
      Upper = O3_upper
    )
)

# Plot monthly CO and ozone concentrations with 95% confidence intervals
plot1 <- ggplot(monthly_plot_data, aes(x = Month, y = Mean, group = Pollutant,
                              color = Pollutant)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper),
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Pollutant, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Carbon Monoxide (CO)" = "seagreen",
      "Ozone (O3)" = "skyblue"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean concentration (ppm)",
    caption = "Points represent monthly means; error bars represent 95% confidence intervals. Data from 2020 are available only from January through April."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```

\pagebreak

## Plot 1: Monthly Mean Concentrations of Carbon Monoxide and Ozone
```{r echo=FALSE}
plot1
```

&nbsp;

CO and ozone concentrations are measured on different numerical scales, so they are displayed in separate panels with independent y-axes. This allows the monthly trends and variation in each pollutant to be clearly visualized without one pollutant's scale obscuring the other.


```{r include=FALSE}
# Add year and month variables
pm25_data <- air_quality_all %>%
  mutate(
    Year = factor(lubridate::year(Date)),
    Month = lubridate::month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE)
  )

# Calculate monthly mean PM2.5 concentrations by year
pm25_monthly <- pm25_data %>%
  group_by(Year, Month) %>%
  summarise(
    PM25_mean = mean(`PM2.5`),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# View monthly summary
pm25_monthly

# Plot monthly mean PM2.5 concentrations by year
plot2 <- ggplot(pm25_monthly, 
                aes(x = Month, y = PM25_mean, 
                    color = Year, group = Year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "2018" = "seagreen",
      "2019" = "skyblue",
      "2020" = "darkblue"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Month",
    y = expression("Mean PM"[2.5]*" concentration ("*mu*"g/m"^3*")"),
    color = "Year",
    caption = "2020 data are available only from January through April."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```

\pagebreak

## Plot 2: Monthly Mean Concentrations of PM2.5 by Year
```{r echo=FALSE}
plot2
```

&nbsp;

A line graph was selected to display monthly PM2.5 concentrations because it highlights changes over time and allows seasonal patterns to be compared across years. Each year is represented by a different colored line, with the 2020 line ending in April because data were only available for the first four months of that year.

\pagebreak

## Interpretation
Monthly CO concentrations were generally highest during the colder months, particularly November through January, and lowest during late spring and summer. In contrast, ozone concentrations were highest during late spring and summer, peaking in June, and lowest during the winter. PM2.5 concentrations varied across months and years, allowing seasonal patterns and differences between years to be compared.
